utterances.text: Unfortunately, there is only a partial hard copy set, and most of the documents are maintained and held either obviously in the vault or for us to consult them, are in software, in soft copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if they are available in soft copy, I wonder whether over the next break we could arrange for a laptop to be made available to the witness so that he can at least bring up the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The soft copy would be a scanned copy of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If the document is in key file, the it would be a scanned copy, but only if the document is in key file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I do understand. Would it be possible -- of course, the Chamber was not very inclined to be presented with a few thousand documents because we wouldn't read them at all. Therefore, we didn't ask them to be filed. But I do understand that there has been either disclosure or they come from the Defence. How have you structured the access to your -- to the documents you disclosed to the Prosecution? I mean, how could you find a document in your set of documents you disclosed to the Prosecution, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence was not able to identify the documents that had ERN numbers given by the Prosecution and that were Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. But how did you organise to have systematical access to your own documents? I mean, if you say, "We can't work with the ERN numbers that were later assigned to the documents."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, according to the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: According to the dates you have the -- yes. So you have them --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. If these are Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. reports -- I apologise. If these are reports, I think that Mr. Philipps could have noticed this. These were chronologically listed by years and dates, and when there are orders and other documents, they are listed by dates, that is, day/month/year, and this is the system the Defence had and this is how we listed our documents and this is how we disclosed them. Now, once the document is given an ERN number the Defence has no use because we have -- we don't know which document this is if we don't have a date. I have raised this on several occasions at meetings with my learned colleague, but we obviously haven't been able to establish a good communication in view of this matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that means that you would be -- do I understand you well, Mr. Philipps, that if you make reference to two sources, that the first one -- that the first date you indicate for Mr. Sipcic, July 1992, that this would have been a document which dates from July 1992, although no specific date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. Or from a witness statement that Tomislav Sipcic was the corps commander in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But if we see, for example, in the -- in your reference to Tomislav Sipcic an ERN number saying "appointment of Mr. Zubic," that would not be a witness statement, that would be a document. Yes. So let's try to see what we can do for the rest of our -- of the cross-examination, see whether with the help of the computer perhaps to be in one way or the other, even if it would be not just a source of refreshment for your memory, because I can imagine that it would not be easy to put that in our system, having your own laptop already attached to our system. I am wondering whether your system would allow if you would attach a small printer to it, to print a copy right away so that we can then put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to ask whether they would be able to set up what would be a key file printer, and the system would have to be attached to part of the OTP network for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it can't be -- I do understand now. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, first of all a suggestion. If Mr. Philipps was to have at his disposal, alongside his chair, the hard copies that do exist, that would be of help. We now have a copy of the document that Ms. Pilipovic has questioned the witness about. In the same fashion, I can arrange for someone here to obtain them as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if Ms. Pilipovic already could provide a list -- I don't know whether you are asking a lot of questions about certain documents, that if you would already give the ERN numbers, because they are related to persons, as in this case with Mr. Sipcic, two possible documents that could be of assistance. So I take it that you have looked in the list whether you can find something in order to see whether you could confront the witness with. Do you have a list of documents you would like to ask questions about?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, again, I have to stress that the documents that the Defence had disclosed cannot be identified with ERN numbers. Specifically, the Defence is interested in a document on the basis of which Mr. Philipps gave his explanation about the operation tactical group, Vogosca. This is one part of the question, for instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but Ms. Pilipovic, you start with Tomislav Sipcic. You start asking about dates. And the report makes clear, and the witness has testified that the sources he used in this respect, that we find them in the annexes. At least there is a fair chance that what you would like to know, you will find them in the ERN numbers that are mentioned in the annexes. If I can find the ERN numbers in 30 seconds and that would be, I think, true for most of the names mentioned, you just look on the list and you see the sources used by the expert, with their ERN numbers. Even if you could not correlate them to your own material, at least we have the ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the problem is that the system, as my learned colleague has already raised, I am repeating, I am reiterating this, that the system that we received from our colleagues is not working in relation to the material that was provided to us on the diskette and has the ERN numbers. We have not been able to identify the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still do not understand. If you are talking about Mr. Sipcic, you will find two ERN numbers in the annex. So I take it that if you want to examine the witness on the sources he used, that at least you look at those documents mentioned in the annex. And as a matter of fact, that is what you are doing, you are asking questions about the appointment of Mr. Zubic. You are asking when was he appointed, is there a signature on it --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you knew what the ERN number is and you could have prepared for that, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have to repeat that the system isn't functioning. The Defence has not been able to open the system and look at the document so that I can conclude from the document whether this was signed by Mr. Sipcic and the date of the document. That is the problem. That is the reason why I asked my question, phrased it in such a way, asking Mr. Philipps whether he knew if this document had been signed by Mr. Sipcic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but now we see that the Prosecution is able to produce the document within a couple of minutes. Did you ask a copy of this specific ERN number to be -- when did you do that? Yes, Mr. Ierace, please respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, they did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then indicate, Ms. Pilipovic, when you asked for a copy of ERN number 07096601-070966.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in order to prepare for the cross-examination of Mr. Philipps, the Defence asked on several occasions, we requested from my learned colleagues certain documents in relation to Mr. Philipps' report. Specifically this document now under this number, the Defence did not ask specifically for this document but we asked for all other documents, and our learned colleagues said that this is quite a voluminous number of documents and that they could not all be disclosed to the Defence. We even asked for it yesterday, but Mr. Ierace told us that he was not able to speak to Mr. Philipps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, twice separately in the last hour Ms. Pilipovic has said to you that she specifically has asked me on a number of occasions at meetings for the dates of the documents supplied by the Defence which are relied upon Mr. Philipps. Mr. President, she went on to say perhaps there was a misunderstanding. Well, indeed, there has been a misunderstanding if she believes she has asked me for those dates. She has, however, repeatedly asked me for copies of all of the documents, and I have replied to her that the documents have already been disclosed to her or have been provided by her to us. Mr. President, had she pointed out to me that she requires the dates of the documents which the Defence has provided and which are listed in the report, then I would certainly have responded that we would have given her those dates. Today, one hour ago, was the first time I became aware of her problem. Over that last hour, I have noticed that it seems, in any event, from the annex to the report, that a number of the references do include either dates or other references. We will now do our best to provide her with copies of documents that she can't locate because there is no date reference, so that she can continue her cross-examination. And perhaps at the end of the next break, or at the beginning, if she has it now, she can provide us with a copy of the ERN numbers of the documents she has not been able to locate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn now. I think it is of little use to continue to hear the one party blaming the other either for not understanding or for not specifically enough asking information. What the Chamber wants is that the cross-examination can take place in such a way that it not be unnecessarily, at least for the future, bothered by the type of incident we dealt with the last 20 minutes. Ms. Pilipovic, you certainly have in mind on what persons you are going to ask questions during the next half an hour or three quarters of an hour. Please find if it is about persons, within five or 10 minutes, and if that is possible, the specific ERN numbers mentioned in respect to that name or in respect of those units you would like to ask questions about and give them, I would say within the next 10 minutes, to Mr. Ierace. And if Mr. Ierace could please see whether someone could retrieve these documents, and at the same time, we try to have the hard copies in court. And if we could do anything with the computer, fine; if not, we at least will try to continue to ask questions about the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I add one further thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I had repeatedly asked the Defence to indicate which parts of this report they dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And there is a more fundamental question in relation to this document. Is it in dispute that Mr. Sipcic was the corps commander on that date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could you please tell us whether that is in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is -- it is not in dispute. It is not contested Mr. Sipcic was the corps commander, but the Defence does not have a document and does not have the exact dates, the exact data until when Mr. Sipcic was the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the exact date of importance for the Defence case? I mean, is it -- if it would have been the end of June 1992 or -- well, apart from we have no date yet, it is not one of the conclusions of this expert. He says, "I found sources in July 1992 and August 1992 that these documents indicate that Mr. Sipcic at that time was corps commander." That is how I understand it. He doesn't say when he became it. Is it of relevance for the Defence case when he became that?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is important for the Defence until when he was the commander, and the Defence does not have this information on the basis of what we have been given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But am I right in understanding, Mr. Philipps, that you have drawn no conclusions as to up to what moment Mr. Sipcic was corps commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no specific date for when he left the post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you have, on the basis of your expertise, you have no specific data that would enable you to tell us when Tomislav Sipcic terminated his office as corps commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. That is also why there is a dotted line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do undertake that you have explained that from the very beginning. Ms. Pilipovic, Mr. Philipps is not here to give the facts. Mr. Philipps is here because on the basis of the facts that he has seen -- on the basis of the documents he has seen and the information he received, he has -- on the basis of the expertise, he has created, according to his expertise, would have been the structure of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. We have had perhaps in the past similar difficulties that you want experts to give us the facts, rather than their expertise. If you would have asked, do you have any additional information which would allow you to tell the Court when Mr. Tomislav Sipcic gave up his position or finished being corps commander, the answer would have been known and we would not have expended 20 minutes. So please keep in mind that whatever, first of all, that try to understand what the role of an expert is, what we can expect from an expert, and that is conclusions structuring the data he had available. Ask him questions about that, not about underlying facts of which he has no knowledge. And please keep that in mind when you make your list of ERN numbers. We will adjourn until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have received a list from the Defence. We will copy the documents. I notice that some of the documents Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. which are requested are documents which have a date and appear to be Defence documents. I make the point only to emphasise that the Prosecution has 13 sitting days left in which to complete its case, and we are anxious that time not be wasted. Mr. President, as I indicated earlier, on a number of occasions, we have asked the Defence to simply indicate which parts of the chart they dispute. They have not done so. Present in court is their expert and, of course, the accused. I think it appropriate that by the time cross-examination is completed, the Trial Chamber clearly understands which parts of the chart are in dispute. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will consider that. Cross-examination will not be finished by a quarter to 2.00, I take it. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic, and I would rather forget about as soon as possible the last 20 minutes and see whether we can constructively proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. The Defence would just like to clarify why it is -- this document of July 1992 and August 1992 is relevant. It is because the Defence has information that in July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... in English at this very moment, or is it my -- I am on channel 4 and I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have technical difficulties, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there are technical difficulties, as far as I understand. I was informed during the break that, before the break, part of the difficulties were due to having only one functioning microphone in one of the booths. Have the -- as soon as the problems have been solved, I would like to be informed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you hear the translation in English now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now hear a voice in English. So let's start to resume -- let's just resume.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one clarification, with your permission. The need of the Defence to have the document of July-August 1992 is because the Defence has unofficial information that Mr. Sipcic was not the corps commander in July and August. And such a document which would now indicate that he was the corps commander in July and August would be important for the Defence because, as of now, the Defence does not have such a document. And I will continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have a copy, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think no one says that Mr. Sipcic was the corps commander. I think that until now - and I don't know what the relevance is - but until now, the expert has testified that on the basis of, as far as I can see, two documents, he has drawn the conclusion that Mr. Sipcic, at the dates of these documents, was the corps commander. So let's try to be very precise and let's try to well understand what an expert can tell us and what an expert cannot tell us. And I see that we have the documents now. So both of the documents are available to you now, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be possible that you continue perhaps on another subject and that the members of the Defence team then perhaps study the documents so that we can continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, regarding your testimony in the chart when you are talking about the assistant corps commander, specifically for morale, logistics, security -- to be more precise, I am talking about slide 7. So when you are talking about Mr. Lugonja, could you please explain to us whether the assistant corps commander for security and for logistics, did I understand it wrongly, we are talking about transcript, page 54, 21, 23, when you are talking about these posts, you are talking about the headquarters sector. Could you please clarify what you said regarding these matters regarding the deputy assistant commander for morale, security, and logistics? Are these people also part of the corps staff?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understand it from the documents, these individuals are part of the corps staff and are heads of specific staff departments. So, for example, Colonel Lugonja was the head of the security and intelligence staff department and Colonel Aleksa Krsmanovic was the head of the logistics staff department.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, when you say "the staff," could you be more specific? Which part of which staff is the sector, as you call it, for morale, security, and logistics?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are all part of the corps headquarters of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, which is divided into various staff sections.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, when you were analysing the documents, did you notice that there is a difference between the corps staff and the corps command?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In some respects there is a command system which functions and the staff are there to facilitate that command. So there is a distinction between a staff officer who has no executive power as a staff officer and an officer who is in command who has executive powers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Philipps. Mr. Philipps, slide number 16, you talked about the operative tactical group, Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, when you were explaining the operative tactical group Vogosca, in the transcript on page 11, 548, lines 12 to 15, you said that it seems that this operational or tactical group was formed in order to achieve better control over the brigades, on the opposite side of Sarajevo from the corps command. Did I understand correctly what you responded in your answer to the question and when you were clarifying the tasks of the Vogosca operational tactical group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understand it, the reason for forming such a group would be so that those brigades could all act together in some way so that improves the command and control of those brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please first clarify for us based on which document you stated that this -- the name of this group is the Vogosca operational tactical group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to refer to my notes and look that up, if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Philipps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On page 18 of 63 of my ERN references, I have various references to reports, including particularly a document, the last on the list, referring to the forming of the TG Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I could understand, Mr. Philipps, you are talking about the Vogosca tactical group.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What I have here is -- I have put Vogosca operational/tactical group, as there seem to be the terms used on several occasions. It is possible, of course, that they are two separate organisations, one a Vogosca operational group the other one a Vogosca tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, when you confirmed for us that the forming of the operational or tactical group Vogosca was with the task of achieving better control on the opposite side of Sarajevo from the corps command, are you in fact telling us that this was a permanent command group, a tactical group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe it was permanent, as I have information about it being reformed at certain times. So my analysis would be that it was formed and reformed at different times, depending on the situation that occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say it was disbanded and formed, can you please tell us, from the period from the 15th of September 1992 up until September 1994, how many times was the group formed and reformed, if you know this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say how many times this formation or re-formation occurred. I only have the fact that it came into existence on a specific date and that it was reformed on another date. So at least two incarnations.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, since you have told us and cited the brigades which comprised the Vogosca tactical group, can you please tell us whether those four brigades which you linked with the diagram -- in the diagram in relation to the Vogosca, so the Ilidza, Rajlovac, Vogosca brigades, so were they part of this group, the Vogosca group, or did this composition change from time to time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understand it, those brigades or parts of those brigades formed part of the operational tactical group at various times. It may be that at one time all of them were part of it or it may be at other times that only some of them or part of each brigade was within the tactical operational group.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you properly that it is your position that these four brigades were practically -- when they were formed, they were always part of the Vogosca tactical group, but this was only a question of how much of each of these brigades would go into the formation of this group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understand it, the first date I have for the formation of the Vogosca operational tactical group was the 15th of September, 1992. Since those brigades existed before that date, I don't think the brigades were formed as part of the group. As far as I can tell, the group was brought together for specific purposes and may have used all the brigade or may have used parts of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, do you have any knowledge about September 1992 when you said that the Vogosca tactical group was formed? Do you know the task why this group was formed? Do you maybe have some information about this in your documents?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be that there is information within my list of documents relating to the reason of the formation of the group. But I was not using that as part of my analysis. So I am afraid I do not know why the group itself, specifically for what combat operation it was formed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So what you are saying, for July 1993, when you say that Mr. Dragan Josipovic was appointed as commander of the Vogosca tactical group, are you -- do you have information for that period when it was formed and why it was formed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just intervene and ask whether those who are listening to the English channel have any translation? I have not really for the last eight lines. So it seems I have a personal technical problem. If there would be anyone who can see why I have a problem -- perhaps there is someone who thinks that I shouldn't listen any more. I think it has changed now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the translation now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear the translation again. So it is the same problem. I will try to read meanwhile, if no one else has a problem. But As soon as someone else has a problem in hearing the English channel, I would like to know. And if the text appears on the screen, even if I would not hear it, I take it that unless anyone informs he that he is not hearing the English channel, I will then read and the problem will be solved after -- during the break. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I understand it, this date of July 1993 falls within the period of the operation known as Lukavac 1993. It may be that the formation of this operation or tactical group or the re-formation of it at this date was related to Lukavac 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, in your analysis of the documents which you analysed in preparation for your expert testimony, did you have available the orders of the commander of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps or a report about the formation or reformation of the Vogosca tactical group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to check which document I referred to, I would have to look at the date relating to my list in the index. But I have a daily report by at that time Colonel Stanislav Galic, which makes me think that refers to the earlier period, rather than to July. So perhaps some of the other documents such as the order by Colonel Dragan Marcetic relating to the forming of the tactical group could refer to that period, but I would need to refer to the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence would like to show Mr. Philipps a document, it is a report, of the command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps signed by Major General Stanislav Galic. It is dated July 7, 1993. Perhaps Mr. Philipps had the opportunity of seeing this document before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Usher, would you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to have a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be wrong to say that I recognise it specifically, but it -- if it is among the Defence documents that were disclosed, then it would be among those documents that I have read when preparing my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have been given a copy of the document accompanied by what appears to be a translation into English. Might I just clarify that the translation is a partial translation, that is, it relates only to numbered paragraph 2 of the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In view of the instructions of the Chamber, we translated only the part that is relevant for us to have the witness clarify that part, so that is under item 2 of this is document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, is this a report, a combat report with the situation at 17 hours, and was it submitted from -- by Major General Stanislav Galic to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. Is that what you conclude from this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It follows the standard format of a report from the corps headquarters to the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, in item 2 of this document we have information that all the units are in full combat readiness and tactical group Vogosca, the Ilidza, and the Igman Brigade are prepared for possible interventions in the direction of attack of the enemy. Mr. Philipps, we have a report here which talks about the tactical readiness of the Vogosca tactical group, is this correct, the combat readiness of the Vogosca tactical group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and of two other brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, when you said "of the two other brigades" as well, am I to conclude that these two brigades did not form a part of the Vogosca tactical group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the wording, I would assume that the tactical group Vogosca, the Ilidza Brigade, and the Igman Brigade were all separate units.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, are we to conclude that the Ilidza Brigade and the Igman Brigade in the period of 1993 -- that is, from this report, could we conclude that the Ilijas and the Igman Brigade were not part of the Vogosca tactical group? Ilidza Brigade and Igman Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be a conclusion from this document on that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On slide 16 of your chart, when you give your explanations and tell us which brigades are part of the Vogosca tactical group, would you agree with me that on the part of the chart where you say that as part of the Vogosca tactical group for 1993 Ilidza Brigade was also included? Would you agree with me that this is perhaps not quite correct when we are talking about this period of time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that particular date, based on this document, it appears that the Ilidza Brigade was not part of the operational tactical group Vogosca, but may have been part of it on another date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, on the basis of your knowledge and information, could you perhaps explain to us, is there a difference between an operational and tactical group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two words mean something quite different; they relate to a level of command. It is possible that the words are confused and are frequently confused in English, but I suspect as tactical military terms they would not be confused in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, could you tell us on which level is the operational group, in your opinion, and on which level is a tactical group, which levels are we talking about? Tactical group Vogosca or operational group Vogosca, what are the levels?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The level normally of an operational group is considered to be at the level of a division or at the level of a multiple number of brigades, whereas a tactical group is much smaller and relates normally to the size of a battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, I would like us to look at slide number 64, please. This is the -- this is about the -- it is the mixed anti-tank artillery regiment. It is that square there. Mr. Philipps, could you repeat for us exactly which units did you include as being part of the 4th Mixed Anti-tank Artillery Regiment.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my diagram I show a series of artillery batteries, in fact, three artillery batteries. Now, a regiment would normally consist of a number of battalions, and each of those battalions would consist of a number of batteries. So, here we are seeing only a very small part of what is in the 4th mixed anti-tank artillery regiment. It is also worth here noting that 155-millimetre Howitzer is not an anti-tank weapon, but an artillery weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, could you tell us on the basis of which documents did you ascertain that as part of the 4th Mixed Anti-tank Artillery Regiment, three artillery batteries are part of that regiment and those artillery batteries that have Howitzers? Mr. Philipps, let us just use the time. Could you perhaps clarify for us what kind of tasks or missions would a mixed anti-tank artillery regiment be used?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid that would fall beyond the scope of my analysis. I can only surmise, which would be of no value.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Philipps.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you like me to answer your previous question?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will need to look up in the index the reference about the artillery batteries.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could assist, it may be on page 4 of the 63-page document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least on page 4, the 4th Mixed Anti-tank Artillery Regiment appears in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The artillery batteries themselves are referred to individually on page 9, there is artillery battery 1, 2, and 3, and that refers to the supplementary index and that relates to a statement with an ERN reference number and a particular page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just in relation to that, the letter that is referred to was filed with the report and gives notice that there is a further document to come. That further document was forwarded to the Defence and copied to the Trial Chamber, I think dated the 31st of May. I don't know that that has actually been formally filed and it should be. But in any event, I think everyone has copy of it. But perhaps I should give notice that I intend to file it at the conclusion of this witness's evidence. Thank you. I should say, tender it, not file it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I refer to ERN 00400589, which was the source. That is a specific page. I happen to have a hard copy of part of that document, if that is of value. It explains that the Howitzers were under corps command and mentions the individual Colonel Jovo Bartula or Bartula Jovo was in charge there. And the relationship therefore between the battery and the commander at that period has been used to identify those batteries.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, could you please tell us the date of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is in fact a transcript of a witness statement taken between the 13th and 19th of May, 1996. And the specific dates of the equipment referred to are simply referred as 1993 and some of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, when you identified these three artillery batteries, that they were part of the 4th mixed anti-tank artillery regiment, could you perhaps tell us for which tasks or missions is the 4th Mixed Anti-tank Artillery Regiment used?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I mentioned earlier that, from my experience, I can surmise what it was used for. I was surprised to see artillery within such a unit which would normally be used for anti-tank purposes. However, the basis of this diagram is the information with which I am provided, and if I am provided with information, then I assess it and put it on to the chart. That is why the batteries themselves have dotted lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, could you tell us what weapons are used, or a part of, for a mixed anti-tank artillery regiment, as far as you know, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would normally expect to find towed anti-tank weapons and other types of anti-tank weapon, such as the T-12 100 millimetre weapon we saw on another diagram and other types of anti-tank missiles, perhaps. This may include various missiles of Russian design. But again, this is really speculation. They are anti-tank weapons, basically.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, are you then saying that Howitzers are not part of a mixed anti-tank artillery regiment? Howitzers, 155 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My detailed knowledge of the order of battle is such that I would not discount the placing of equipment in an unusual position just because, in a standard way, you would not expect to find it. For within the organisation of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, I have found several pieces of equipment in places where I would not expect to find them. And, therefore I did not discount the fact that Howitzers could be within an anti-tank artillery regiment, even though they are not for the purposes of anti-tank fire. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, do you have any other information on the basis of which you believe this to be the way a mixed anti-tank artillery regiment is organised, that is, all the elements that this 4th Mixed Anti-tank Artillery Regiment consists of?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could have spent some time looking at the structure of this organisation when it -- when it was previously part of the JNA. But I felt that this would not be helpful, as I was studying a separate entity to what was the 4th Corps of the JNA, and the Sarajevo Romanija Corps is not the 4th Corps of the JNA. It contains elements of it, but to extrapolate what was in the 4th Corps into what is in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, I felt would not have been helpful or, indeed, accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, when you were speaking about the Ilijas Brigade, you said that it was a brigade with the largest number of soldiers. Could you tell us, on the basis of the documents, what was the front line, how long was the front line of the Ilijas Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid my analysis did not cover exactly the lengths of front lines of organisations. It really only covered the structure of those organisations and their rough position in and around Sarajevo. It is worth here noting that the Ilijas Brigade had a front facing away from, mostly away from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, when you were anaylsing the documents and you created this structure, you worked on the structure of the Ilijas Brigade, did you find in documents and information that a Mrakovo Battalion is mentioned in any of these documents?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not found a specific mention of the Mrakovo Battalion itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, could you tell us, if you know, who issues orders to a commander of a section within a fire group of a battalion where mortars are included? Do you have such knowledge? Who is giving orders to the commander of a mortar section?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would be grateful if -- the way the question is presently phrased, it is not clear what sources of knowledge,

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a quarter to 2.00. Ms. Pilipovic, I did understand that your question was to be understood as a very general question, such as, would under these circumstances, and if so, what would be similar to what the witness testified before, is what would you expect under normal circumstances. I think that is how I understood the question. If I am wrong, then please tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that clarifies that issue, but I would seek a redaction of part of the transcript for the last few minutes, for reasons that may become apparent to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then could you please specifically mention pages and lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should that be from 88, 24, until 89, 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, we will adjourn until tomorrow after I have dealt with the redaction. Could you give us an indication on how much time you would need for your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we will need another half an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Another 30 minutes. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if that is the case, then perhaps I should amend the timetable. The intention was to call Mr. Karavelic tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But if we are confident that we can conclude cross-examination and re-examination of Mr. Philipps within say an hour, then I would be happy to finish off Mr. Philipps at this point tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that would be possible for you, Mr Philipps. I think it would also be the best for your expert, Ms. Pilipovic. utterances.text: [Interpretation] But just to say that for the French transcript on page 69, line 9, I don't think that the documents in question were preserved in the vaults of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
